subject: Post-demo: Support runbook + data governance checklist
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Elena Duarte <elena@finsight.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@finsight.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Support runbook + data governance checklist

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Per our conversation, I put together a short follow-up with the items you asked to validate around PII handling, retention, logging, and support access (RBAC + break-glass). I attached a draft runbook and a one-sheet retention matrix for quick review.

Short recap of asks we captured:
- Which classes of PII you consider sensitive for FinSight (PII types + processing contexts).
- Retention windows by data category and any legal/regulatory minimums.
- Required logging/audit detail (request-id, user-id mapping, redaction expectations).
- Support access model: who can request temporary elevated access, approval flow, and telemetry for break-glass events.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) You review the attached runbook_v1 and retention spreadsheet and mark any items that are inconsistent with your policies (due: 2026-12-10).
2) Rishi will follow up with specifics on our RBAC primitives (roles, least-privilege defaults, and elevation TTL).
3) We’ll schedule a short technical workshop (30–45 min) with your security/infra team next week to walk controls and integration points.

A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- Data residency: hosted Redwood API can pin region (US/EU) at the tenant level; we support single-region tenancy for your account if required.
- Retention: by default we retain request logs for 30 days; we can extend to 1–7 years for audit purposes under Dedicated/Private plans with an agreement.
- Support access: standard flow is ticket -> manager approval -> short-lived role (1 hour) with full audit log + post-mortem. Break-glass is supported and emits an immutable event with sign-off.

Attaching: redwood_support_runbook_v1.pdf (draft runbook), redwood-data-retention-summary.xlsx, diagram-infra-access-paths.png

Thanks — I’ll coordinate timing for the workshop once you confirm availability.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the materials. A few quick points from our security team after skimming:
1) PII scope: we classify account-holder name, email, SSN (tokenized), payment identifiers, and transaction descriptions as sensitive. We’ll send a formal list.
2) Retention: we need logs tied to financial transactions retained for 7 years for compliance, but request-level debug traces can be kept 90 days. Will confirm exact policy.
3) Support access: question — do break-glass events require two approvers, or can they be escalated to an on-call manager for emergency approvals?

We’re available for a workshop on Wed 12/9 (afternoon ET) or Thu 12/10 (morning ET).

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Duarte <elena@finsight.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@finsight.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Support runbook + data governance checklist

Elena — quick technical answers to your question and a few details to help your team evaluate: 

- Break-glass approvals: configurable. Default Redwood flow is single approver (on-call manager) for speed; we can require a 2nd approver for high-sensitivity accounts or specific actions (e.g., access to decrypted PII). This is a per-tenant policy toggle in Dedicated/Private.

- Elevation model: temporary roles are issued via our token service with TTLs (default 60 minutes) and scoped permissions. Elevation requests are recorded and stored in the audit log with a snapshot of active sessions.

- Audit/logging: request-level logs include request_id, route, model, user_token_hash, and timestamp. We can add request payload hashes and encrypted user identifiers if you need stronger mapping without storing raw PII. These logs can be shipped to your SIEM (syslog/forwarder) or stored in an S3-compatible bucket with lifecycle rules that match your retention policy.

- Data residency & retention: for 7-year retention per your needs, we recommend Dedicated with long-term archival to your account’s encrypted object store. We can provide the retention automation (lifecycle rules) and certificate of disposal when retention period ends.

I’ll attach a short appendix for RBAC roles and common mappings (SR-roles.txt) to the runbook before the workshop.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
